findings.title: On VT1, a simple model from other labs beats the current production model
findings.summary: Compared test by test, the research model places VT1 about 10 mL/min closer to the experts than the current production model, and is better in 7 of 12 labs, although it never saw any of them and the production model had seen most. On VT2 the two are level. Averaging the two models' answers brought VT2 a few mL/min closer than either alone, a lead still to test on models that never saw the test's lab.
findings.method: The same held-out tests scored by both models, each lab held out in turn; the uncertainty range of the per-test difference, from resampling whole recordings within each lab, stays below zero on VT1 and crosses zero on VT2.

findings.title: A model trained on other labs carries to a new one
findings.summary: A simple model trained only on other labs, given each test's ventilation and gas-exchange signals on a common intensity axis, places VT1 about 40 mL/min and VT2 about 20 mL/min closer to the experts than a cohort-typical guess, on labs it never saw. It holds in 10 or 11 of the 12 labs, cycling and running, clinical and athletic, and matches the current production model without having seen any of those labs.
findings.method: Gradient-boosted trees; each lab held out in turn; three random seeds, which agree within 2 mL/min; the gain's uncertainty range stays clear of zero on both thresholds.

findings.title: On treadmill tests, the research model halves the production model's VT1 error
findings.summary: Split by how a test was run, the research model's VT1 error on treadmill tests is about 170 mL/min, against about 330 for the current production model and 470 for a cohort-typical guess. On cycle ergometers the two models are level. It is a split looked at after the fact, on few treadmill tests, so it is a lead to test on its own, not yet a result.
findings.method: Errors from the held-out predictions of the three-seed model, grouped by the ergometer recorded in each test's load channel.

findings.title: Experts disagree, and how much depends on the lab
findings.summary: When two experts mark the same test, their VT1 readings sit about 90 to 340 mL/min apart depending on the lab, and their VT2 readings about 70 to 220. A model that found the true threshold would still sit roughly 0.7 times that gap from each expert, so that floor, not zero, is what a model is judged against.
findings.method: Tests read independently by several experts, in six labs: the mean gap between two readings of the same test.

findings.title: Textbook breakpoints corroborate; they do not detect
findings.summary: Run automatically over the exercise phase, the classical V-slope and ventilatory-equivalent breakpoints place both thresholds further from the experts than a cohort-typical guess. They are worth showing beside a result, as evidence to inspect, not as the answer.
findings.method: No tuning; scored on the same tests and in the same way as the models.

findings.title: A model is only as good as the signal it is handed
findings.summary: Given breath-by-breath rows instead of the one-second series it was built on, the current production model placed VT2 about 40 mL/min further from the experts. The service already resamples every upload, so users were never affected. Every model is now measured exactly as production feeds it.
findings.method: The same model and tests, scored through both inputs.

findings.title: One benchmark for every idea
findings.summary: Every result is measured the same way: on labs a model never trained on, against a cohort-typical guess, the current production model and the gap between experts. The benchmark reproduces our earlier reference figures exactly, so old and new numbers compare.
findings.method: Twelve labs, each held out in turn; two more sealed for final checks; uncertainty from resampling whole recordings within each lab.

timeline.title: Research and production models averaged
timeline.outcome: A small VT2 gain, kept as a lead: half of the average had seen the test labs.

timeline.title: Research model against production, test by test
timeline.outcome: Better on VT1, level on VT2.

timeline.title: Tree model, three seeds
timeline.outcome: Held under resampling: the transfer result became robust.

timeline.title: Production model re-measured through its own input
timeline.outcome: Overturned an earlier result, now corrected.

timeline.title: Tree model on binned signals
timeline.outcome: Beat a cohort-typical guess on every threshold, on unseen labs.

corrections.text: An early run reported the production model as worse than a cohort-typical guess on VT2. The benchmark had handed it the wrong input. Re-measured the same day, it is better, and the claim was withdrawn before anyone relied on it.

phases.note: The first phase benchmark is next in the queue.

efficiency.note: From now on every experiment records model size, training compute and how many labelled tests it learned from.
